1.title: Resources, Resource Groups, Subscriptions and Management Groups
1.text: Welcome to Module five: Resources, Resource Groups, Subscriptions and Management Groups. It covers the exam area Describe Azure architecture and services. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. Describe Azure resources and resource groups. Describe subscriptions. Describe management groups. Describe the hierarchy of resource groups, subscriptions, and management groups. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Describe Azure architecture and services (thirty-five to forty percent). Exam format: forty-five minutes; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official A Z nine hundred study guide, current skills measured.

1.title: The four levels
1.text: The four levels. Azure organizes everything in a hierarchy from the top down. Management group. What it is: A container for subscriptions. Main purpose: Apply governance (policy, access) to many subscriptions at once. Subscription. What it is: A unit of management, billing and scale. Main purpose: Billing boundary and access-control boundary. Resource group. What it is: A logical container for resources. Main purpose: Group resources that share a lifecycle.

1.title: The four levels, continued
1.text: The four levels. Resource. What it is: An instance of a service (a V M, a storage account, a database). Main purpose: The thing you actually use.

1.title: The four levels, continued
1.text: The four levels. The figure shows this: The Azure hierarchy: management groups, subscriptions, resource groups, resources.

1.title: Resources
1.text: Resources. A resource is a manageable item available through Azure: a virtual machine, a storage account, a web app, a database, a virtual network. Each resource. Is created in one resource group and lives in one region. Has a type, a name and properties. Is managed through the Azure Resource Manager (Module thirteen).

1.title: Resource groups
1.text: Resource groups. A resource group is a logical container that holds related resources for a solution. Key facts (very testable). Every resource is in exactly one resource group. A resource group cannot be nested inside another resource group. You can move resources between resource groups (with some limits). Deleting a resource group deletes all the resources in it. Resources in one group can be in different regions; the group has a location only for its metadata. You can apply access control, policy, tags and locks at the group level, and they are inherited by the resources inside it.

1.title: Resource groups, continued
1.text: Resource groups. Resources that share a lifecycle (created, updated and deleted together) belong together. Exam tip: "Delete everything for a project in one step" to delete the resource group. Exam tip: Remember three boundaries: the subscription is the billing boundary, the resource group is the lifecycle boundary, and the management group is the governance boundary across subscriptions.

1.title: Subscriptions
1.text: Subscriptions. A subscription is the agreement and boundary for using Azure services. It provides authenticated and authorized access to resources. Billing boundary. Costs are produced and invoiced per subscription. Access-control boundary. Access can be granted at subscription level and inherited down. Scale boundary. Each subscription has limits and quotas.

1.title: Subscriptions, continued
1.text: Subscriptions. Reasons to use more than one subscription. Environments: development, test and production. Organizational structure: different departments with their own budgets. Billing: separate invoices per team or project. Limits: a subscription has resource limits and quotas. A subscription trusts one Microsoft Entra tenant (Module nine) for identities, while one tenant can have many subscriptions. A Free account gives limited free services and a credit for a trial period.

1.title: Management groups
1.text: Management groups. Management groups sit above subscriptions and let you manage access, policy and compliance across many subscriptions. Policy and access applied to a management group are inherited by every management group, subscription, resource group and resource below it. There is a root management group at the top of the directory. A hierarchy can have up to six levels of depth (not counting the root level or the subscription level). Each management group and each subscription has one parent. Example: a company applies a policy "allowed regions" to the top management group so every subscription follows it.

1.title: The hierarchy and inheritance
1.text: The hierarchy and inheritance. Azure Policy assignment. Where: Management group. What happens: All subscriptions beneath must follow it. Role assignment (R B A C). Where: Subscription. What happens: Applies to all resource groups and resources within. Lock or tag. Where: Resource group. What happens: Inherited by resources inside the group. Exam tip: Settings flow downward. A role granted at a management group reaches every subscription under it; a role granted on a resource reaches only that resource. Start broad and make exceptions narrow.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Fabrikam Outdoors wants to apply one policy to twelve subscriptions at once. Where should it assign the policy? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: A management group above the subscriptions. Management groups sit above subscriptions and pass policy and access down to everything beneath.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A project is finished and the team wants to delete all of its resources in one operation. What should it delete? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: The resource group that holds them. Deleting a resource group deletes every resource in it.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. Which statement about resource groups is true? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Resources in a group can be in different regions. The group's location stores metadata only; its resources can be in other regions. A resource is in exactly one group, groups cannot be nested, and deleting a group deletes the resources.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. A company wants separate bills for its marketing and engineering teams. What is the simplest design? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: One subscription per team. A subscription is a billing boundary, so separate subscriptions give separate invoices.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. A role is assigned to a user at the subscription level. What happens to the resource groups in that subscription? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: They inherit the role assignment. Role assignments are inherited downward to resource groups and resources.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. What is at the top of the Azure management hierarchy? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: The root management group. The root management group is the top; management groups contain subscriptions, which contain resource groups, which contain resources.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Put the four levels in order, top to bottom. Answer: Management group, subscription, resource group, resource. Question two. What does a subscription act as for costs? Answer: A billing boundary. Question three. Can a resource group be inside another resource group? Answer: No.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What happens when you delete a resource group? Answer: All its resources are deleted. Question five. Which level lets you apply policy to many subscriptions? Answer: Management group. Question six. Do settings applied at a higher level flow down or up? Answer: Down (inheritance).

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Order: management group to subscription to resource group to resource. Resource group: logical container; one group per resource; no nesting; delete group equals delete resources. Subscription: billing, access-control and scale boundary; trusts one Entra tenant. Management group: above subscriptions; policy and R B A C inherited; root group at the top. Inheritance: flows downward; apply broad rules high, exceptions low. In the next module, we continue the course.
